narrative.northStar: The Phone, and As Little Else As Possible
narrative.overview:
The console has three panes. A 232px sidebar lists your phones, each as a thumbnail, a name and one word. A fluid stage shows the selected phone at full viewport height inside a real night bezel, under a one-line header. A 340px panel shows one thing at a time: how to connect an agent, or what the agent did. The owner said the previous build "looks AI generated" and asked for it to be simple, so the simplification removed everything that called attention to itself: the nav block, counts, pills, status dots, ID lines, tabs, timeline nodes, footers and icon cards. What remains is text in four sizes, 1px hairlines, ink buttons and one held violet, spaced on one scale.

Light is the default. Dark follows the system until the person picks a theme with the toggle, and the choice is stored on `<html data-theme>`. Both themes share one structure and change only token values. Night objects (the bezel, the boot screen, the code block) stay dark in both themes, because they depict hardware and terminals, not page surfaces.
keyCharacteristics: Three panes with the phone first: 232px sidebar, fluid stage, 340px panel; one column at 960px and below.
One spacing scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48) and four type sizes (12, 14, 18, 24) inside the console.
State is a word, not a dot. The only dots are the live-stream pulse under the phone and the amber waiting pulse in the panel.
Violet is for links, focus, text selection and control mode, nothing else.
Flat: 1px hairlines and tonal steps; the input focus ring is the only shadow.
Light and dark from one token set; night objects never invert.
Motion is functional and switches off entirely under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Violet-Is-Interaction Rule
rules.body: Violet marks links, focus, text selection and the person's own control of the phone, and nothing else. It never fills a button and never marks a selected row (selection is a wash). As a fill it is only a tint: the 8% hover wash on link buttons. The 30% radial glow on the auth statement panel is the one held exception.

rules.name: The Words-Carry-State Rule
rules.body: A phone's state is one lowercase word. Only "working" (green-ink) and "failed" (red) take a color; every other word is muted. There are no status dots: the only dots in the console are the live-stream pulse under the phone and the amber waiting pulse in the panel, and each sits beside words that say the same thing.

rules.name: The Night Object Rule
rules.body: The bezel, the boot screen and the code block stay night in both themes. Their tokens deepen slightly in dark but never invert. The page theme never reaches inside a phone or a code block.

rules.name: The Twin Block Rule
rules.body: Dark values are declared twice in globals.css: in `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` on `:root:not([data-theme="light"])`, and on `:root[data-theme="dark"]`. Any change to a dark token edits both blocks identically.

rules.name: The Four Sizes Rule
rules.body: Inside the console, type is 12, 14, 18 or 24px. Hierarchy comes from those four steps, from weight (400, 500, 600) and from ink against muted. Only the auth screen uses a display clamp.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Machine Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono marks values a machine produces or reads: phone IDs, the MCP config and shell exports, the API key and its mask, file and variable names in inline code, and `kbd`. Activity times are mono too, so the time column lines up. Mono is never used for headings or decoration.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Regions separate with a 1px line or a tonal step, never a shadow. The only lines thicker than 1px are the two violet outlines, the 2px ink underline on the selected client tab, and the 2px boot and booting-thumbnail bars.

rules.name: The Real Bezel Rule
rules.body: Device frames are drawn in container-query units on the `.dash-live` container, so the bezel scales with the screen at any size. iPhone: a 402:874 screen, frame radius 16.5cqw, screen radius 13.2cqw. Android: a 540:1200 screen, frame radius 11cqw, screen radius 8cqw. Both pad the screen by 3.4cqw inside a bezel-colored frame with a 1px bezel-ring edge. Every depiction of a device (sidebar thumbnail, narrow chip, stage skeleton) keeps the true screen ratio for its platform.

rules.name: The Shared Mark Rule
rules.body: The viewfinder logo (`.logo`, `.logo-mark` with `::before`/`::after` corner brackets and a rotated 6px center square) is a binding brand asset whose markup and CSS are shared verbatim with the landing app. Never redraw, restyle or approximate it. It draws in `var(--ink)`, so it follows the theme. To tint it, set `--ink` on a parent, as the boot screen does with boot-mark; never edit the mark. Load-bearing dependency: the box-sizing reset **must** cover pseudo-elements (`*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }`), because the corner brackets are pseudo-element borders and break under `content-box`.

rules.name: The Quiet Thumbnail Rule
rules.body: A sidebar thumbnail is one frame taken from the phone's `/stream` socket, after which the socket is closed (it gives up after 8 seconds). It never uses the screenshot RPC, because RPC calls land in the action log as if the agent had acted. Opening `/stream` also counts as activity and keeps a phone alive, so a frame is taken only right after an agent action, never on a timer: the refresh key changes at most once per 15-second window, and only while the last agent action is less than 60 seconds old. An idle phone keeps its last frame and is never kept alive by its thumbnail.

rules.name: The Kill-Switch Rule
rules.body: `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` sets `animation: none` and `transition: none` on everything, with `!important`.

dos: **Do** keep the live phone the largest thing in the first viewport: size it from viewport height inside the 232px / fluid / 340px shell.
**Do** take spacing from 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32 and 48px, and type from 12, 14, 18 and 24px, inside the console.
**Do** say a phone's state in one lowercase word, coloring only "working" (green-ink) and "failed" (red).
**Do** define every new color as a token in the light `:root` and in both dark blocks, and reference roles (`var(--ink)`) in components.
**Do** keep bezels, boot screens and code blocks night in both themes.
**Do** draw devices in container-query units at the platform's true screen ratio (402:874 iPhone, 540:1200 Android).
**Do** guard destructive actions in two steps (arm, relabel, red fill, confirm; disarm after 4 seconds; "Closing…" while it runs).
**Do** take sidebar thumbnails as one `/stream` frame right after an agent action, and at no other time.
**Do** give every secret and snippet a copy button that announces through `aria-live`, and mask tokens on screen while copying the real value.
**Do** collapse to the top bar at 960px, visually hiding the wordmark and the "Phones" heading rather than removing them, and keep `?section=` deep links and `aria-current`.
**Do** keep the dependency posture: next, react, react-dom, geist and @vercel/analytics only; inline stroke SVG icons (15px, 1.4 stroke, currentColor); no icon packages.
donts: **Don't** redraw or restyle the shared logo mark, or narrow the box-sizing reset; tint the mark only by setting `--ink` on a parent.
**Don't** add status dots, count pills, badges, counted tabs, timeline nodes, icon cards or panel footers; the simplification removed them on purpose.
**Don't** fill a button, mark a selection or color a heading with violet.
**Don't** let the page theme invert a bezel, boot screen or code block.
**Don't** refresh thumbnails on a timer or through the screenshot RPC; a timer keeps idle phones alive, and the RPC writes fake agent actions into the log.
**Don't** use faint for text a person needs to read; it is for marks.
**Don't** introduce shadows, hover lifts, uppercase or tracked labels, or a fifth type size inside the console.
**Don't** show closed or errored sessions among the phones; they belong to Usage.
**Don't** edit one dark token block without the other.
**Don't** import landing CSS or its dark/violet world; the console and landing are separate worlds sharing only the logo and voice.
